The '''Airy processes''' are a family of [[Stationary process|stationary]] [[stochastic process]]es that appear as limit processes in the theory of [[random growth model]]s and [[random matrix theory]]. They are conjectured to be [[Universality class|universal limits]] describing the long time, large scale spatial fluctuations of the models in the [[Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation#KPZ universality class|(1+1)-dimensional KPZ universality class]] (Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation) for many initial conditions (see also [[KPZ fixed point]]).

The original process Airy<sub>2</sub> was introduced in 2002 by the mathematicians [[Michael Prähofer]] and [[Herbert Spohn]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Michael|last1=Prähofer|first2=Herbert|last2=Spohn |title=Scale Invariance of the PNG Droplet and the Airy Process |journal=Journal of Statistical Physics|publisher=Springer |volume=108 |date=2002 |issue=5–6 |page=1071 |doi=10.1023/A:1019791415147 |arxiv=math/0105240 |bibcode=2002JSP...108.1071P }}</ref> They proved that the height function of a model from the (1+1)-dimensional KPZ universality class - the [[PNG droplet]] - converges under suitable scaling and initial condition to the Airy<sub>2</sub> process and that it is a stationary process with [[almost surely]] continuous sample paths.

The Airy process is named after the [[Airy function]]. The process can be defined through its [[finite-dimensional distribution]] with a [[Fredholm determinant]] and the so-called '''extended Airy kernel'''. It turns out that the one-point marginal distribution of the Airy<sub>2</sub> process is the [[Tracy-Widom distribution]] of the [[Gaussian unitary ensemble|GUE]].

There are several Airy processes. The Airy<sub>1</sub> process was introduced by [[Tomohiro Sasomoto]]<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/38/33/l01|date=2005|publisher=IOP Publishing|volume=38|number=33|pages=L549–L556|first1=Tomohiro|last1=Sasamoto|title=Spatial correlations of the 1D KPZ surface on a flat substrate|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General|arxiv=cond-mat/0504417}}</ref> and the one-point marginal distribution of the Airy<sub>1</sub> is a scalar multiply of the Tracy-Widom distribution of the GOE.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Riddhipratim|last1=Basu|first2=Patrick L.|last2=Ferarri|title=On the Exponent Governing the Correlation Decay of the Airy1 Process |journal=Commun. Math. Phys.|publisher=Springer |date=2022 |doi=10.1007/s00220-022-04544-1|arxiv=2206.08571}}</ref> Another Airy process is the Airy<sub>stat</sub> process.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/cpa.20316|date=2010|publisher = Wiley|first1=Jinho|last1=Baik|first2=Patrik L.|last2=Ferrari|first3=Sandrine|last3=Péché |title=Limit process of stationary TASEP near the characteristic line|journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics|volume=63|number=8|pages=1017–1070|hdl=2027.42/75781|hdl-access=free|arxiv=0907.0226}}</ref>

The Airy<sub>1</sub> resp. Airy<sub>2</sub> processes can be thought of as the limit behavior of [[Asymmetric simple exclusion process|TASEP]] fluctuations with flat resp. step initial condition.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Borodin | first1=Alexei | last2=Ferrari | first2=Patrik L. | last3=Sasamoto | first3=Tomohiro | title=Transition between Airy<sub>1</sub> and Airy<sub>2</sub> processes and TASEP fluctuations | journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics | date=2008 | volume=61 | issue=11 | pages=1603–1629 | doi=10.1002/cpa.20234 | arxiv=math-ph/0703023 }}</ref>

== Airy<sub>2</sub> process ==
Let <math>t_1<t_2<\dots <t_n</math> be in <math>\R</math>.

The '''Airy<sub>2</sub> process''' <math>A_2(t)</math> has the following finite-dimensional distribution
:<math>P(A_2(t_{1})<\xi_1,\dots,A_2(t_{n})<\xi_n)=\det(1-f^{1/2}K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}f^{1/2})_{L^2(\{t_1,\dots,t_n\}\times \R)}</math>
where
:<math>f:=f(t_j,\xi)=1_{\{(\xi_j,\infty)\}}(\xi)</math>
and <math>K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}:=K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}(t_i,x;t_j,y)</math> is the ''extended Airy kernel''
:<math>K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}(t_i,x;t_j,y):=\begin{cases}{\displaystyle \int_0^\infty e^{-z(t_i-t_j )}\operatorname{Ai}(x+z)\operatorname{Ai}(y+z)\mathrm{d}z}& \text{if }\;t_i\geq t_j,\\
{\displaystyle -\int_{-\infty}^0 e^{-z(t_i-t_j)}\operatorname{Ai}(x+z)\operatorname{Ai}(y+z)\mathrm{d}z}&\text{if }\;t_i< t_j.\end{cases}</math>

=== Explanations ===
* If <math>t_i=t_j</math> the extended Airy kernel reduces to the Airy kernel and hence
::<math>P(A_2(t)\leq \xi)=F_{2}(\xi),</math>
: where <math>F_{2}(\xi)</math> is the Tracy-Widom distribution of the GUE.
* <math>f^{1/2}K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}f^{1/2}</math> is a [[trace class operator]] on <math>L^2(\{t_1,\dots,t_n\}\times \R)</math> with counting measure on <math>\{t_1,\dots,t_n\}</math> and Lebesgue measure on <math>\R</math>, the kernel is <math>f^{1/2}K^{\operatorname{ext}}_{\operatorname{Ai}}(t_i,x;t_j,y)f^{1/2}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Kurt|last1=Johansson |title=Discrete Polynuclear Growth and Determinantal Processes |journal=Commun. Math. Phys. |volume=242 |date=2003 |issue=1–2 |page=290 |arxiv=math/0206208|publisher=Springer |doi=10.1007/s00220-003-0945-y |bibcode=2003CMaPh.242..277J }}</ref>
